title: Python SDK: incremental chat callbacks and event-bridge cookbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Ship a compact, well-documented cookbook and API adapter set for the Python SDK that makes building production-grade streaming chat integrations ergonomic for application engineers. The focus is on: (1) a minimal callback adapter that surfaces typed event objects, (2) an "event-bridge" utility to translate raw stream frames into higher-level signals (choices, partial tokens, tools, errors), (3) graceful cancellation and deterministic finalization hooks, and (4) a set of runnable examples and migration notes for customers using earlier iterator/callback patterns.

Background: We have many internal examples that rely on iterators, checkpointing, or heavyweight consumer adapters. Customers repeatedly ask for a small set of patterns that work with asyncio and sync code, provide clear retry semantics, and interoperate with observability (span hooks, token counts). This ticket consolidates those patterns into a cookbook plus an officially supported adapter in the SDK.

Acceptance criteria: 
- API: publish a new Python helper module "redwood.sdk.streams.event_bridge" with two public entry points: SimpleCallbackAdapter and EventBridge. Both must have synchronous and async usage examples. 
- Documentation: cookbook page with three runnable examples: (A) low-latency UI consumer using on_token callbacks, (B) background worker that records structured events to logging/metrics, (C) tool-invocation pattern where tool payloads are emitted as distinct events. Each example includes failure/retry recommendations. 
- Ergonomics: callbacks receive typed event tags ("token", "choice_end", "tool_call", "meta_error", "complete") rather than raw strings. Finalization hook fires with aggregated token counts and final choice metadata. 
- Retries: define and document idempotency semantics for retrying streaming requests when intermittent network errors occur; provide helper to resume from last stable event when feasible. 
- Tests: unit tests for adapter logic, fuzz tests for out-of-order frames, and an integration example that runs against the staging streaming endpoint. 
- Telemetry: add optional hooks to emit per-event telemetry points without forcing users to use our tracing library. 

API sketch (non-normative): 
- class SimpleCallbackAdapter(on_event: Callable[[Event], None], on_final: Optional[Callable[[FinalSummary], None]]=None)
- async for ev in EventBridge(stream): yields Event objects (for advanced users)
- helpers: resume_from_checkpoint(checkpoint_id) and stable_event_boundary(records)

Migration notes: map old iterator patterns -> new callback calls, provide quick diff in cookbook. Include a small snippet showing converting a for-await loop to SimpleCallbackAdapter with equivalent backpressure behavior.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: customers expect perfectly resumable streams; reality: many models and intermediate proxies drop state. Mitigation: document limits and provide best-effort resume helper that uses emitted choice boundaries and idempotency tokens. 
- Risk: API surface creep. Mitigation: keep public API surface small (two entry points) and mark advanced utilities as experimental.

Testing plan: unit tests for event classification, simulate partial frames and injected errors, end-to-end runbook using staging endpoint. Performance smoke: measure per-token callback overhead and keep <5% added CPU overhead on typical UI patterns.

Deliverables: new module in sdk/python, docs/cookbook markdown in docs site, three runnable examples in examples/streams/, unit + integration tests, a small migration guide for customers.

Notes and links: Drive doc: https://drive.google.com/example-cookbook (private), GH draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/9999 (draft), staging telemetry dashboard: https://grafana.internal/streams-bridge (internal), related issue ENG-61111 (streaming consumer contracts).
